title: Babul Supriyo Calls Kolkata Diwali Double as Kali Puja Coincides
excerpt: Filmibeat reported Babul Supriyo calling Kolkata's Diwali a double celebration because Kali Puja falls the same night; he also recalled his last Diwali with his mother in 2020.
body:
• Singer and West Bengal minister Babul Supriyo described celebrating Diwali in Kolkata as celebrating two festivals together — a double Diwali — in Filmibeat's report.
  • The two festivals are Diwali and Kali Puja, also called Shyama Puja, which fell together on Sunday, November 8, 2026, on the Kartik new-moon night.
  • Supriyo's most cherished Diwali memory, in the syndicated summary of his comments, is his last Diwali with his mother in 2020, before her passing during the COVID pandemic.
  • For readers marking the season: in Kolkata the same night centres on Goddess Kali at temples such as Kalighat and Dakshineshwar, alongside Diwali lamps.

For Babul Supriyo, Diwali in Kolkata is not one festival but two at once. Filmibeat reported the singer and West Bengal minister describing it as celebrating two festivals together, and therefore a double Diwali. The second festival is Kali Puja — the worship of Goddess Kali that Bengali Hindus observe on the same Kartik new-moon night as Diwali.

Two festivals, one night

That coincidence is not rhetorical. Views Bangladesh reported Hindus celebrating Shyama Puja and Diwali, two major religious festivals, together on Sunday, November 8, noting that Shyama Puja is also known as Kali Puja or Dipannita Kali Puja and is observed annually on the new moon night of the Bengali month of Kartik. Devotees worship Goddess Kali while households light lamps for Diwali, both carrying the message of light overcoming darkness, the report said. Many families also observe Lakshmi Puja on the same day, it added.

"The second festival is Kali Puja — the worship of Goddess Kali that Bengali Hindus observe on the same Kartik new-moon night as Diwali."

A personal memory at the centre

Supriyo's comments were personal as much as festive. A syndicated summary of his Diwali recollections says he cherishes his last Diwali with his mother in 2020, a moment he described as deeply significant before her passing during the COVID pandemic. His connection to the festival, the summary says, is rooted in his upbringing in Kolkata at his ancestral home, which it describes as having a 400-year history, with family traditions maintained there for 171 years.

The lesson he drew

Beyond the memories, Supriyo offered advice to aspiring artists, drawing a parallel between the festival of lights and the dualities of life. The summary of his comments says he stressed that success warrants celebration while failure provides experience for growth, advised artists to "keep the fire burning inside," and said that navigating darkness can illuminate the value of light.

Why Kolkata feels different

In most of India, Diwali's main night centres on Lakshmi Puja. In Kolkata and across Bengal, the same night belongs also — and for many households primarily — to Kali. That is the substance behind Supriyo's double Diwali line: one evening of lamps, crackers and family ritual carrying two distinct pujas, which is why the festival in his home city runs deeper than a single celebration.

How the shared night is observed

Views Bangladesh described how the joint festival is marked: Shyama Puja's main rituals are generally performed around midnight, devotees offer prayers to Goddess Kali at temples and puja mandaps, and many people light lamps at homes, temples and cremation grounds in memory of deceased parents and relatives. Illumination, aarti and prayers run through the night — the same lamps that, for Diwali, carry the message of light overcoming darkness. It is that layered observance, Kali Puja at midnight inside a Diwali night of lamps, that Kolkata households experience as one continuous festival rather than two separate dates.
